conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be part of your care team. You’re here because of right upper belly pain, fever, and fatigue. Can you tell me more about what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for about four days now I’ve had a low fever, mostly in the evenings, and this dull ache under my ribs on the right side. I feel really tired and nauseous, but no vomiting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any chills? Changes in urine or stool? Chest pain or cough?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Chills, yes. But no chest pain, no cough, no diarrhea or constipation. Urine’s been normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You were just treated for cholangitis earlier this month with meropenem, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I finished that course about two weeks ago. I thought I was over it, but now this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given your history, we’re concerned this could be another flare of cholangitis. We’ll run some blood tests and get an ultrasound to check your liver and bile ducts.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need another ERCP like last time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. We’ll see what the tests show. If there’s a blockage or infection, we might consider it later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs came back. Your bilirubin is elevated at 2.0, and alkaline phosphatase is high—339. That fits with bile duct issues. White count is normal, though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So is it cholangitis again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. We’re starting you on meropenem again, just in case. Better safe than sorry with your history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m on a PICC line for antibiotics at home—should we use that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll use your PICC. We’ve ordered a liver ultrasound for tomorrow morning to get more details.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. The ultrasound showed no bile duct dilation, which is reassuring. But there’s mild ascites and two stones still in the gallbladder remnant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The stones again? Could they be causing this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly, but they’ve been there before without symptoms. We’re not sure they’re the main issue. We’re ordering a CT scan today to rule out abscess or other complications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: How’s the CT looking?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No abscess or fluid collection. Your liver shows cirrhosis and varices, which we expected. There’s mild thickening in the colon wall—could be from portal hypertension. But no clear source of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So not cholangitis?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re not certain. No fever now, and cultures are negative. But given your history, we’re continuing meropenem for five days as a precaution.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds—can I keep taking them?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re continuing your home meds: ursodiol, rifaximin, omeprazole, and the others. We held your diuretics for now since you’re not retaining fluid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood and urine cultures came back negative. No bacteria grew. Respiratory virus test was also negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So nothing’s causing the fever and pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely a mild flare related to your PSC. The infectious disease team reviewed your case and agreed it’s not classic cholangitis this time. But we’ll finish the antibiotic course to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad it’s not serious. What about my transplant status?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re still listed. Your MELD score is stable at 9, so no urgent change. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re looking better. No pain, no fever. Your repeat labs show bilirubin down to 1.4 and alkaline phosphatase improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly by tomorrow. We’ll restart your diuretics—furosemide and spironolactone—at home doses. And you’ll finish the antibiotics at home via PICC.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been itchy again. Can I take more hydroxyzine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you can take your usual 50 mg at night. Cholestyramine also helps with itching—keep taking that daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge tomorrow. Your exam is normal, labs are stable, and you’re feeling well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What about follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your liver doctor next week. Also, they want a colonoscopy soon because of the colon wall changes and your anemia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had two poor preps before. Should I worry?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just do your best with the prep. It’s important for screening, especially with your history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Final labs look good. White count is a bit low at 3.3, but stable. No signs of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from the antibiotics?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Possibly. We’ll monitor it. Your hemoglobin is down a little—10.1—so keep an eye on energy levels.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been tired, but not dizzy or short of breath.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. Stay hydrated and keep eating well. Your albumin is low—3.0—so protein intake is important.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need another PICC line after this?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, this one can stay for now. We’ll coordinate with home health for your antibiotic infusions.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home. We’re discharging you with a five-day course of meropenem, and all your regular meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the diuretics—same as before?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, furosemide 40 mg twice daily and spironolactone 100 mg twice daily. Watch for swelling or shortness of breath.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And no beta blocker because of how I felt on nadolol?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Correct. You reported dizziness and chest pressure, so we’re not restarting it. Your last endoscopy showed no varices, so it’s okay for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel much better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Call if you develop fever, pain, or confusion. Otherwise, see you in clinic soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And thank you for explaining everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Of course. Take care, and we’re glad you’re feeling better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—should I avoid gluten completely?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, absolutely. You have celiac disease, so even small amounts can cause issues. Stick to your gluten-free diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And thyroid medicine every morning?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, levothyroxine on an empty stomach. Same with your other daily meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And escitalopram for my mood—I’ve been feeling better there too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. Keep taking it daily. Mental health is just as important.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll make sure to follow up on everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll send all the details to your husband too, so he’s in the loop.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: He’ll be glad to hear I’m going home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We are too. Rest up, and don’t hesitate to call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. Take care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye for now.
